check: whether the S1B items recorded as unfinished are still unfinished
whyItMatters: Several documents are annotated with items that were open when written. Left unqualified they read as current gaps, and the previous round showed one of them - S1C-DRAIN-01 - no longer reproduces.

itemTheAllocationWhichWasCalledUnfinishe.docText: T0/compiled byte limits are checked, but peak object occupancy, full reservation before allocation, and long-term pin behaviour still need pressure verification; do not substitute a logical estimate for a measured memory ceiling.
itemTheAllocationWhichWasCalledUnfinishe.whatCoversItNow: ReservationHeapPressureTest, 107 lines, one @Test with a 180-second timeout
howItMatchesPointByPoint: peak occupancy: samples heap usage through a scheduled sampler while eight concurrent pins hold real payloads, and reads pool peak usage via getPeakUsage
full reservation before allocation: asserts terrain.reserved() is 64 MiB and compiled.reserved() is 32 MiB while the payloads are live, not after
long-term pin behaviour: eight pins are held simultaneously and the record type Pinned keeps real tiles and component voxels alive, with the assertions checking they are non-empty rather than stubs
release: asserts both reservations return to zero after the pins close
itemTheAllocationWhichWasCalledUnfinishe.measuredNotEstimated: The test records sampledHeapPeak and heapPoolPeakSumNonSimultaneous alongside the reserved ceilings, which is a measurement rather than an estimate - the distinction the doc text explicitly asks for.

itemStillGenuinelyOpen.rampFourCandidates: S1B records that fixed four-candidate ramp selection and the full outer-edge guard are unfinished. No four-candidate concept exists anywhere in src/main, and the three RampSpecificationTest cases cover geometry rather than candidate selection, so this remains open as described.
itemStillGenuinelyOpen.waterGateRemainderMerging: Recorded unfinished and not contradicted by anything found.

conclusion: One of the two items checked has been closed by later work and the documents do not say so; the other is still open exactly as described. Distinguishing them requires reading the tests, not the annotations.
